cells.tense: The pen is in your hand now, and the small routine at the bench is running well.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Keep the door open next time you sit down to the practice. Let someone nearby watch you do it, and when they say something, don't wave it off. Then go back to work.
cells.core:
Two things get carried in the same routine, and it doesn't tear: the thing that needs a little attention most days, and the thing that needs a lot right now. You go to the bench and do the small motion, and the bigger demand gets held too, because the small one is steady. You'd probably call it nothing.

So none of it gets seen. Not modesty exactly — the routine feels like housekeeping, too plain to bring up. Still, you can do one piece of it where someone nearby can watch. Keep the door open when you sit down. If they say something, don't wave it off; let the sentence finish. Then go back to work. The routine doesn't get heavier for being seen. It gets something under it.
cells.sheetLine: The small routine carries two things, and carries them well.
cells.verb: tending what is growing with steady hands, a little at a time
cells.place: alone at the bench with the same small routine, repeating it

cells.tense: You are already braced for a future where this practice has to be sharper than it is.
cells.act: use the finished thing for an hour instead of improving it
cells.ask: Take the piece you've already made well — the one that keeps getting tweaked instead of used — and put it to use for an hour without touching it. No refinements. Just the use.
cells.core:
The practice is running ahead of where it stands. Something is good enough to use, and it keeps getting improved instead, because a finished thing reads as a risk that isn't handled yet. One more pass, then one more, and each pass is smaller and the grip is tighter. This isn't care pretending to be care. It's care that has stopped letting the thing be done.

Take the piece you've already made well — the one that keeps getting tweaked instead of used — and put it to use for an hour without touching it. No refinements. Just the use. The hour will feel wrong at first, then it won't. What you're testing is whether a finished thing can sit there finished. If something in you says nothing is finished yet, that's worth noticing without acting.

cells.tense: You are still at the threshold of a practice you already set down and left there.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Choose one small motion of the practice — five minutes, the version you first learned — and do it this week just as it was, with no plan for what it becomes. One motion, once.
cells.core:
The practice has gone quiet. You can picture the bench, you know how the small daily motion feels in your hands, and none of it is happening. That's the position: not lost, not ruined, just unmoving. Whatever made you want it hasn't gone. It's harder to reach, that's all.

Choose one small motion of the practice — five minutes, the version you first learned — and do it this week just as it was, with no plan for what it becomes. One motion, once. That may be the whole shape of it for now: a single repetition, no arc, no rebuilding. Repetition is how this was built the first time, and the first time wasn't impressive either. A small thing can be lit and stay small.

cells.tense: You are at the bench already, calling the daily work ordinary while it is not.
cells.act: let what you gave up be seen by the people it was for, without a word about it
cells.ask: Next time the practice is what's holding something up, let whoever it's for sit with you while you do it for a few minutes, and say nothing about why. Then carry on.
cells.core:
The daily work holds up more than your own skill. Whatever you've built at the bench is carrying something for someone, maybe a few people, and your account of it is that you just do your little thing. From where you sit it reads like a hobby. From where they sit it's load-bearing.

Next time the practice is what's holding something up, let whoever it's for sit with you while you do it for a few minutes, and say nothing about why. Then carry on. Nothing has to be explained, then or later. What changes is only that the time you gave up is no longer invisible to the person it was for. The work stays the same size. Someone just gets to see it.
